what_this_is_not: R values are copied from the tracked fixture. Julia values are computed fresh by tools/true_parity_julia_receipts.jl, which repeats the computation of the cited twin test with the same inputs and settings; R was not run and is not recomputed here.

cases.julia_source: StatsAPI.deviance(fit), as called at test/test_postfit_twins_p1.jl:63; fit as at test/test_postfit_twins_p1.jl:52
cases.note: Rank-2 Gaussian fit on UNCENTRED data (trait means 0.5, -0.3, 0.2, 0.8, -0.6, 0.1; sha256 checked); R: value ~ 0 + trait + latent(0 + trait | unit, d = 2, unique = FALSE) converged with a positive-definite Hessian; same optimum (logLik within 1e-6, asserted in the test). The R values are far from zero (smallest |value| about 0.058) and pairwise distinct, so a constant or zero implementation fails. The postfit batch fixture these rows replace was row-centred (R values ~1e-14). Julia's deviance is -2 logLik; R's is read from deviance(fit), so the comparison is R's own deviance against that identity, not a copy of the log-likelihood guard.
